reviewers.summary: The new regular-mode Data Room wiring silently rejects case selection before a current scene snapshot exists. The walk test also leaves the required follow-camera behavior unasserted.

findingList.message: The regular-mode Data Room cannot select a case before a current Hangar snapshot exists. The new test currently expects selection not to occur in this state, which conflicts with the acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The regular-mode Data Room passes sharedHangarAircraftSelectionHandler as onConfirm. That handler returns when canAdmitHangarCommands(hangarSnapshot) is false; the regular-mode view is shown before a current Hangar snapshot exists.
evidence.failureScenario: After signing in, when a user activates a listed case before entering the Hangar, hangarSnapshot is null and selection is silently ignored, contrary to the criterion that activating an entry selects the case.

findingList.message: The named App-host test does not verify that ArrowUp changes the follow-camera pose, or that the camera stays unchanged while follow is off. It can pass with broken camera behavior.

evidence.codePathTraced: The App-host test asserts that ArrowUp changes the avatar, but reads only the static text "Camera pose" and never checks the element's data-hangar-camera-pose value.
evidence.failureScenario: If the App stops updating the follow-camera pose after an accepted ArrowUp, this named behavior test still passes, so it does not prove the camera behavior required by the criterion.

reviewers.summary: The previous findings are resolved: the regular-mode Data Room is rendered, the App exposes a focusable walk region, and the named App-host tests are present. The new camera test does not verify the camera movement required by its criterion.

findingList.message: The walk and follow-camera test does not assert that ArrowUp changes the camera pose.

evidence.codePathTraced: The App updates the camera pose after an accepted ArrowUp step, but this test only reads the constant text 'Camera pose' and checks that it exists; it never compares the pose before and after the step.
evidence.failureScenario: If the camera update is removed while avatar movement still works, this test passes without verifying the acceptance criterion that ArrowUp changes the follow-camera pose.

reviewers.summary: The previous-round composition findings are addressed. The changed App-host test still does not assert the camera state behavior required by the first acceptance criterion.

findingList.message: The named App-host test does not verify the follow-camera behavior required by the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test reads only the constant text `Camera pose` and checks that it is defined; it never asserts the camera pose value before or after ArrowUp, or that toggling follow affects only camera state.
evidence.failureScenario: If the App stops updating the follow-camera pose on ArrowUp, or the Follow avatar control changes avatar state, this acceptance test still passes.
